title: Attica: high-level design
subtitle: Local development stack as the repository runs it today, read from the code and environment/overview.md on 2026-10-24
lede: What runs when Attica runs, from the browser on the left to the data on the right. Four of these boxes are processes started by hand: Redis, the Django backend under Daphne, the Vite dev server and the outbox worker.
version_line: Version 1, 2026-10-24: 10 boxes, 10 arrows. Read from /home/molef/Work/attica at commit a85cc0c plus its uncommitted working tree.

details.heading: Where each box comes from
lines: Vite dev server: frontend/vite.config.js lines 16 to 25, the proxy for /api, /vendors, /cart, /checkout and /ws.

Django backend: one Daphne process serving main.asgi:application, holding the REST API (rest_framework in INSTALLED_APPS, JWT through rest_framework_simplejwt) and the WebSocket consumers (channels; chat/consumers.py, notifications/consumers.py). The chat consumer saves each message to SQLite before broadcasting it.
SQLite: DATABASES in settings.py line 156. Every app writes here through the Django ORM, including bookings, chat messages and the scheduling_outboxevent rows the worker reads.
Uploaded media: MEDIA_ROOT in settings.py line 226; 50 MB cap at line 230.
Webhook targets: SCHEDULING_WEBHOOK_TARGETS = [] in settings.py line 239; delivery by urllib in _dispatch_webhooks_for_event.
Sentry: settings.py lines 247 to 257, skipped when SENTRY_DSN is unset.

details.heading: How to read the lines
lines: A solid line is a request that waits for an answer. A dashed line is asynchronous (the channel layer, the worker polling its table). A dotted line only carries traffic when a setting turns it on: Sentry needs SENTRY_DSN and webhooks need a configured target.

details.heading: What is not drawn
lines: Stripe appears only as comments in vendors/views.py and as an MCP for future work, so it has no box. There is no Celery, no object storage and no CDN.
The booking-request write path stores its notification row and never pushes it to the channel layer (scheduling/services.py, _create_in_app_notification), so no line runs from the worker to Redis.
node-websocket/ holds only node_modules and a lockfile, so it is not a running component.
Inside the Django backend box sit the REST API, the WebSocket consumers and the Django admin. Splitting it is the next diagram one level down.
